 Baby Brezza Recalls Popular Baby Bottle Dryer for Possible Overheating 
 Follow Sales & Shopping News View feed Baby Brezza Recalls Popular Baby Bottle Dryer for Possible Overheating 
 Here’s what to do if you have one.
 By Marisa LaScala Published: Nov 10, 2026 10:48 AM EST Save Article Share Article We've been independently researching and testing products for over 120 years. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission. Learn more about our review process. 
 2 min read Automatic bottle washers, dryers, and sterilizers can be a boon to anyone with an infant in the house, since they make it quick and easy to clean a baby bottle and get it right back into the rotation again. But the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) has just issued a recall on a popular dryer/sterilizer model, and the company is offering replacements to families who have it.
 The dryer is the Baby Brezza SuperFast Sterilizer Dryer, which has an issue with getting too hot. “The recalled sterilizer dryers can overheat when plugged in and operating, posing a risk of injury from a burn hazard if the surface is handled,” the CPSC notes. About 29,000 units were sold in the United States, and another 4,500 were sold in Canada. While no injuries have been reported, there have been more than 30 reports of overheating or the plastic housing melting.
 How to tell which Baby Brezza dryers were affected
 According to the CPSC, families should check the label on the bottom of the unit. The recalled units have model numbers BRZ0083, BRZ0154, and BRZ0156. 
 These were sold in stores at T.J. Maxx and Marshalls, and online at several different retailers, including Target, Babylist, and babybrezza.com. The recalled units were sold from January 2024 through October 2026.
 What to do if you have a recalled dryer
 Those who have purchased the recalled dryer should stop using it immediately (but don’t throw it out just yet).
 After that, Baby Brezza is issuing no-cost replacements, including shipping. 
 In order to get the replacement, customers are asked to unplug the unit, cut the power cord, and take pictures of the destroyed unit, including the model number. They’ll also have to go to the Baby Brezza recalls page, where they will also be asked to fill out a recall form. The return authorization number from the recall form and the photos should be sent to recall@babybrezza.com . After the form is filled out and the photos are uploaded, it’s then OK to dispose of the unit.
 For more information on the replacement process, customers can call 888-527-9824 from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday, email recall@babybrezza.com , or visit babybrezza.com .
 It’s also a good idea to register any products in order to be notified of any recalls, or keep an eye on CPSC.gov for any other recalls and safety alerts.
